भारतीय नौसेना को पहला स्वदेशी बहु-उद्देशीय पोत 'समर्थक' सौंपा गया

लार्सन एंड टुब्रो लिमिटेड (एल&टी), कट्टुपल्ली द्वारा निर्मित पहला स्वदेशी बहु-उद्देशीय पोत (एमपीवी) 'समर्थक', 27 अगस्त 2026 को भारतीय नौसेना को सौंपा गया। 

इस जहाज में 75 प्रतिशत से अधिक स्वदेशी सामग्री का इस्तेमाल हुआ है और इसे एक बहु-उपयोगी परीक्षण और मूल्यांकन प्लेटफॉर्म के तौर पर तैयार किया गया है।

साथ ही, इस जहाज को समुद्री निगरानी और टोह लेने, अपतटीय गश्त करने और जरूरत पड़ने पर मानवीय सहायता व आपदा राहत कार्यों में मदद करने के लिए डिज़ाइन किया गया है। 

इस जहाज का नाम बहुत सोच-समझकर 'समर्थक' रखा गया है, जिसका अर्थ है 'समर्थन करने वाला'। यह नाम कई मिशनों में भरोसेमंद मददगार के तौर पर जहाज की भूमिका को दर्शाता है।

Optional-PSIR Paper-1-2026

SECTION-A

1. Write on the following in about 150 words each: (10 × 5 = 50 Marks)

* (a) Resurgence of political theory


* (b) Post-colonial theory of State


* (c) The freedom of the pike is death to the minnows.


* (d) Legitimacy is always a 'social construct'.


* (e) Herbert Marcuse turned Freudianism on its head in his critical theory.



2.

* (a) "Rights of the man are separate and independent of the State." Critically analyze the perspective of Laski. (20 Marks)


* (b) "Fortune favours the brave." In the light of this statement, discuss Machiavelli's concepts of 'virtue' and 'fortune'. (15 Marks)


* (c) Discuss B. R. Ambedkar's views on democracy and State socialism. (15 Marks)



3.

* (a) Mill's work was crucial to the development of liberalism, because it straddled the divide between classical and modern theories. Analyze. (20 Marks)


* (b) Wollstonecraft developed first systematic feminist critique. Discuss her main ideas. (15 Marks)


* (c) Discuss Gandhi's approach to property in relation to trusteeship. (15 Marks)



4.

* (a) "Representative democracy is not an absolute principle, rather a question of time, place and circumstances." Analyze the statement. Mention the major challenges to representative democracy. (20 Marks)


* (b) What is capability approach? Elaborate the distinctive features of the capability theory of equality. (15 Marks)


* (c) Analyze Kautilya's Saptanga theory. How do you explain its significance in present-day politics? (15 Marks)



---

SECTION-B

5. Answer the following in about 150 words each: (10 × 5 = 50 Marks)

* (a) How did Swadeshi grow into a demand for Swaraj?


* (b) The Constitution of India was secular even before the word was included in the Preamble. Comment.


* (c) Identity has become an important phenomenon in the modern politics in India. Discuss.


* (d) Ending proxy leadership in Panchayati Raj is a necessary step towards true grassroots democracy. Comment.


* (e) Discuss the impact of liberalization on agriculture sector in India.



6.

* (a) From passive resistors to armed revolutionaries, the Indian Freedom Struggle has a strong imprint of women freedom fighters. Elucidate. (20 Marks)


* (b) When there are multiple stakeholders of power, conversation and consensus become the natural ingredients of governance. Analyze with respect to coalition politics. (15 Marks)


* (c) Evaluate the Centre-State relation with reference to Article 293 and analyze its implications for the Indian federal structure. (15 Marks)



7.

* (a) Elucidate the prominent trends in voting behaviour in contemporary India, and discuss how astroturfing affects the scenario. (20 Marks)


* (b) Highlight any five constitutional provisions that restrain the powers of the executive, and evaluate their effectiveness in current times. (15 Marks)


* (c) Map the different types of ethnic conflicts that have emerged in 21st century India. (15 Marks)



8.

* (a) Discuss the causes and consequences of inter-State water disputes in India. (20 Marks)


* (b) Critically comment on the shifts in the functioning of the Indian Parliament in the last two decades. (15 Marks)


* (c) "The lack of political will in preventing environmental degradation is one of the major challenges that India is experiencing." Comment. (15 Marks)

गांवों में डिजिटल इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर मजबूत करने की दिशा में कदम, सरकार ने ‘दानवीर’ पहल के जरिए मांगा जन सहयोग

पंचायती राज मंत्रालय ने ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों में डिजिटल इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर को मजबूत बनाने के लिए आम नागरिकों की भागीदारी बढ़ाने की दिशा में एक नई पहल शुरू की है।

मंत्रालय ने लोगों से ‘दानवीर’ बनने का आह्वान किया है। यह एक जन-सहभागिता-आधारित कंप्यूटर क्राउडसोर्सिंग पहल है, जिसके तहत व्यक्ति और संस्थाएं सत्यापित ग्राम पंचायतों को सीधे डेस्कटॉप कंप्यूटर दान कर सकते हैं। 

पंचायती राज मंत्रालय के अनुसार, ‘दानवीर’ पहल का उद्देश्य ग्राम पंचायतों में डिजिटल सुविधाओं को मजबूत बनाना और सरकार द्वारा संचालित विभिन्न कार्यक्रमों, विशेष रूप से राष्ट्रीय ग्राम स्वराज अभियान (आरजीएसए) के तहत उपलब्ध कराए जा रहे बुनियादी ढांचे (इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर) को पूरक सहयोग प्रदान करना है

Optional-Geography-2026 Paper1

SECTION 'A'

1. Answer the following in about 150 words each: (10 × 5 = 50 Marks)

* (a) What is 'Helical' flow How Helical flow accounts for meander modifications? (10 Marks)
* (b) Define 'pseudo monsoon' and explain its spatial distribution (10 Marks)
* (c) How are seamounts and Guyots the same and different? Comment. (10 Marks)
* (d) How a 'Solum' as a concept different from 'Pedon'? Describe. (10 Marks)
* (e) With suitable examples describe the hazards of flood plain settlement. (10 Marks)

2.

* (a) "Environmental geomorphology deals with the impact of natural landforms and processes." Elucidate with suitable examples. (20 Marks)
* (b) Discuss the potential consequences of the collapse of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) for the world. (15 Marks)
* (c) "Overgrazing has become an alarming situation of bioloss in many bio-geographical regions of the world." Illustrate with examples. (15 Marks)

3.

* (a) Describe the general characteristics and structure of a thunderstorm and suggest suitable classification of thunderstorm. (20 Marks)
* (b) Anthropogenic impacts have caused major global and regional changes and imbalances in ecosystem. Elucidate with examples. (15 Marks)
* (c) What is scarification? List out various impacts and examples of scarification on land. (15 Marks)

4.

* (a) How does the annual variations in temperature and precipitation influence plants growth, development and distribution? How do animals cope up with variations in climate? (20 Marks)
* (b) Examine the importance of axis of dilation of airmasses in frontogenesis and the origin of Temperate cyclones. (15 Marks)
* (c) Construction of large dams poses serious challenges. Describe the threats and solutions associated with it. (15 Marks)

---

SECTION 'B'

5. Answer the following in about 150 words each: (10 × 5 = 50 Marks)

* (a) "Systematic Geography is essentially analytical and makes generic concepts and Universal Laws." Elucidate with examples. (10 Marks)
* (b) Critically examine the significance of five functioning forms with regard to agricultural regions of the world proposed by D. Whittlesey. (10 Marks)
* (c) "The majority of migrants go only a short distance." Explain with examples. (10 Marks)
* (d) "Sustainable development requires Intergenerational and Intragenerational equity." Comment with examples. (10 Marks)
* (e) "Under what situations Von Thunen's model of agricultural location is still rational." Justify with examples. (10 Marks)

6.

* (a) Discuss the Geometry of Land Values in Urban Community and delimiting the Central Business District (CBD) in detail. (20 Marks)
* (b) Analyse the measuring patterns of settlement in relation to the nearest Neighbour Index and Rank-Size-Rule in detail. (15 Marks)
* (c) Write an essay on disease and global warming according to the report of Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC). (15 Marks)

7.

* (a) What are the main concerns of radical geography? Describe the salient features and objectives of radicalism in geography. (20 Marks)
* (b) Discuss agricultural productivity and techniques adopted for computing efficiency in the levels of agricultural productivity. (15 Marks)
* (c) Elaborate partition of Indian subcontinent and international migration in detail. (15 Marks)

8.

* (a) What are the principles of urban planning? Critically analyse town planning in India in the post independence period. (20 Marks)
* (b) What are the approaches of human development? Describe in detail the measures for computing human development index. (15 Marks)
* (c) Explain the Rimland Theory with reference to ongoing geopolitical scenario in the world. (15 Marks)

राष्ट्रीय कृषि और ग्रामीण विकास बैंक (नाबार्ड) और राष्ट्रीय अवसंरचना वित्तपोषण विकास बैंक (नैबफिड) ने ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों पर महत्वपूर्ण प्रभाव डालने वाली बुनियादी ढांचा परियोजनाओं के वित्तपोषण में सहयोग मजबूत करने के लिए एक प्रारंभिक समझौता किया है। 

दोनों संस्थानों ने संयुक्त बयान में कहा कि समझौता ज्ञापन संयुक्त वित्तपोषण, ज्ञान साझा करने और वित्तपोषण के नए समाधान विकसित करने के लिए एक रूपरेखा प्रदान करता है।

Optional-Anthro Paper1-2026

SECTION-A

1. Write notes on the following in about 150 words each: (10 × 5 = 50 Marks)

* (a) Health as a cultural construct
* (b) Canalization and catch-up growth
* (c) Myth as oral literature
* (d) Ethnoarchaeology and classical archaeology
* (e) Genetic polymorphism and natural selection

2.

* (a) What is meant by a somatotype? Discuss the Heath-Carter anthropometric method, giving its advantages over that of Sheldon's method. How can somatotyping be applied in sports sciences? (20 Marks)
* (b) How do religious beliefs help people to devise cultural mechanisms to adapt to their environment? Discuss in detail with appropriate examples. (15 Marks)
* (c) How is the theory of structuralism helpful in understanding the concepts of caste and gender? (15 Marks)

3.

* (a) How do the concepts of power, authority, legitimacy and social control change with changing political organization? Discuss in detail giving suitable examples. (20 Marks)
* (b) Human evolution is a product of both biological and cultural factors. Elaborate. (15 Marks)
* (c) Give the distribution of Palaeolithic sites around the Himalayan and Sub-Himalayan areas, highlighting the typo-technologies of the tools. (15 Marks)

4.

* (a) Discuss the phylogenetic status, characteristic features, geographical distribution and lifeways of *Paranthropus*. (20 Marks)
* (b) Discuss 'incest taboo' as the basis of development of kinship systems in human societies. (15 Marks)
* (c) Numerical chromosomal aberrations can be due to abnormalities in autosomes as well as sex chromosomes. Elaborate in terms of the effects these have on human body, giving suitable examples. (15 Marks)

---

SECTION-B

5. Write notes on the following in about 150 words each: (10 × 5 = 50 Marks)

* (a) Ethics in anthropological fieldwork
* (b) Distinguishing features of nuclear and mitochondrial DNA
* (c) Feminist movement and family
* (d) Anthropometry in ergonomics
* (e) Thermoluminescence dating method

6.

* (a) How would you find out that a particular disease/disorder is inherited and, if so, in which manner? Elaborate with suitable examples. (20 Marks)
* (b) Critically discuss how culture determines human behaviour in the light of Leslie White's theory. (15 Marks)
* (c) What are Strepsirhini Primates? Describe their geographical distribution and mention the characteristics that distinguish them from Haplorhini Primates. (15 Marks)

7.

* (a) Discuss the mixed method approach in anthropological research. (20 Marks)
* (b) What do you understand by fertility and mortality? How are these influenced by biological and socio-ecological factors? (15 Marks)
* (c) Write a detailed note on the characteristic features, chronology, geographical distribution, tool types and lifeways of Magdalenian cultural tradition of Europe. (15 Marks)

8.

* (a) Compare Edmund Leach's structuralism with interpretive anthropology of Clifford Geertz. (20 Marks)
* (b) In what manner is our understanding of serogenetics and cytogenetics useful in reproductive biology? What are the major ethical issues involved in reproductive technology? (15 Marks)
* (c) Discuss, with appropriate examples, how basic personality types may lead towards building up of national character. (15 Marks)

हिंडाल्को ने कर्नाटक में भारत का पहला सुपरफाइन पीपीटी एटीएच प्लांट शुरू किया

हिंडाल्को इंडस्ट्रीज़ ने 27 अगस्त 2026 को कर्नाटक के बेलगावी में एक नई मैन्युफैक्चरिंग यूनिट शुरू की है, जो देश में अपनी तरह की पहली यूनिट है। 

यह प्लांट 'सुपरफाइन प्रेसिपिटेटेड एल्युमीनियम ट्राईहाइड्रेट' (PPT ATH) बनाता है। यह एक खास मटीरियल है जिसका इस्तेमाल बड़े पैमाने पर इलेक्ट्रिकल केबल और इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर के पार्ट्स को आग से सुरक्षित बनाने के लिए किया जाता है। 

बेलागावी में बनी नई फ़ैसिलिटी की सालाना प्रोडक्शन क्षमता अभी 30,000 टन है। यह क्षमता वायर और केबल इंडस्ट्री से मिलने वाली फ़ायर-सेफ़ केबल की भारत की लगभग पूरी घरेलू मांग को पूरा करने के लिए काफ़ी है।

हिंडाल्को ने इस प्लांट को इस तरह से प्लान किया है कि देश में मांग बढ़ने पर इसे चरणों में बढ़ाकर 60,000 टन तक किया जा सके।
